entry.literal_statement:
Let $a,b$ be nonnegative integers with $a<b$, and let $[s_{2^a1^b}]_{3,n}$ denote the coefficient of $s_{2^a1^b}$ in the Schur expansion for the $(3,n)$ case. Write $[r]_{q,t}$ for the corresponding $q,t$-analogue used in the paper. **The recursive coefficient conjecture.** 
$$
[s_{2^a1^b}]_{3,n}=(qt)[s_{2^a1^{b-3}}]_{3,n-3}+\sum_{i=0}^{a}[b+i]_{q,t}.
$$
 The formula is proposed for the coefficients with $a<b$ as a way to compute the remaining $(3,n)$ Schur expansions; no proof or resolution is supplied here.

entry.title: Dodgson-intersection model conjecture for nonzero $c_2$-invariants
entry.literal_statement: A $c_2$-invariant has a minimal model if it is represented by a projective variety of smallest possible dimension, and a Dodgson intersection is the variety defined by an intersection of Dodgson polynomials. **Dodgson-intersection conjecture.** Every non-zero $c_2$ has a minimal model which is a Dodgson intersection. This conjecturally identifies the geometric form underlying every nonzero graph-theoretic $c_2$-invariant, but no general proof is known.

entry.title: The maximum-row-size conjecture for prefix-reversal generating triples
entry.statement:
For integers $n$ and $k$ with $n>k+1$, define 
$$
F_k(n)=\{m:k<m<n,\ \langle r_n,r_m,r_k\rangle=\operatorname{Sym}_n\}.
$$
 **Maximum-row-size conjecture.** 
$$
\max_{n>k+1}|F_k(n)|=\begin{cases} k+1&\text{if }k\text{ is even},\\ \frac{k+1}{2}&\text{if }k\text{ is odd}. \end{cases}
$$
 The conjecture is motivated by computational experiments and the displayed generating-triple patterns; the source gives no proof or resolution.

We now proceed to describe some tools from group theory that are used in the proofs of our results. Let G be a finite group acting on a finite set \Omega . The G -orbit of x\in\Omega , or simply the orbit of x , denoted by \mathcal{O}(x) , refers to the set \mathcal{O}(x)=\{g(x):g\in G\} . A G -invariant set is a union of G -orbits. The action is said to be transitive on \Omega if for each x,y\in\Omega there is g\in G such that g(x)=y . A nonempty subset B\subseteq\Omega is called a block of imprimitivity (or simply a block) for the action if for every g\in G either g(B)=B or g(B)\cap B=\varnothing , where g(B)=\{g(b):b\in B\} . There are at least two block systems for every action: \{x\} for x\in\Omega and \Omega itself, and one refers to these as trivial blocks. entry.title: The $K_5$ conjecture for $\phi^4$ prime ancestors
entry.statement:
A $\phi^4$ prime ancestor is a prime ancestor arising in $\phi^4$ theory, and $c_2^{(q)}(G)$ is its $c_2$-invariant at the prime power $q$. **The $K_5$ conjecture.** The only $\phi^4$ prime ancestor with

$$
c_2^{(q)}\equiv-1\mod q
$$

for all $q$ is the complete graph $K_5$. This was verified computationally in the ranges reported in the paper, but the unrestricted assertion remains open.

entry.title: Universal dimension bound for primitive graph $c_2$-invariants
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a primitive graph with first Betti number $h_1(G)$, and let $\dim(c_2(G))$ denote the dimension of a minimal model of its $c_2$-invariant. **Universal dimension-bound conjecture.**

$$
\dim(c_2(G))\leq2h_1(G)-11.
$$

The bound is stated to be sharp at loop order $8$ for $P_{8,41}$, but its general validity remains open.
entry.analysis: Source defines c2 through point counts divided by q^2 modulo q, with models over varying fields. Minimal model dimension is not computably certified by one finite-field sweep. Low-loop negative RHS would be a domain defect, excluded.

entry.title: Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture for independent position chromatic numbers
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $\overline{G}$ be its complement, and choose $\pi\in\{\operatorname{gp},\operatorname{mp}\}$, where $\operatorname{gp}$ and $\operatorname{mp}$ denote general and monophonic position, respectively. Let $\chi_{\pi_{\rm i}}(G)$ denote the chromatic number whose color classes are independent $\pi$-position sets. **Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{\pi_{\rm i}}(G)+\chi_{\pi_{\rm i}}(\overline{G})\leq n+1.
$$

The survey identifies this as an open problem; no general proof or counterexample is reported.

entry.title: Fitzpatrick's fractional general position conjecture for square grids
entry.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, let $P_n\mathbin{\square}P_n$ be the $n\times n$ Cartesian grid, and let $\operatorname{gp}_f$ denote the fractional general position number. For even $n\geq 3$, define the lower bound from Theorem 2.1 by

$$
\frac{n^2-2t(t+1)}{n-t-\frac12}
$$

for $0\leq t\leq n/2$. For odd $n\geq 3$, use the two lower bounds from Theorem 2.2, namely

$$
\frac{n^2+1-8k^2}{n-2k}
$$

and

$$
\frac{n^2-1-8(k^2+k)}{n-2k-1}
$$

with the parameter ranges specified there. **Fitzpatrick's conjecture.** The lower bound from Theorem 2.1 is optimal for even $n$, and the bound from Theorem 2.2 is optimal for odd $n$.

Exact values were known in the survey only for small orders, although the lower bound had been shown best possible through $n=10$; the conjectured optimality for all even and odd orders remains open.

entry.title: Kruft's lower general position number conjecture for Cartesian products
entry.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, let $G\mathbin{\square}H$ denote their Cartesian product, and let $\operatorname{gp}^-(G)$ denote the lower general position number of $G$. **Kruft's conjecture.** For any graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
\operatorname{gp}^-(G\mathbin{\square}H)\geq\min\{\operatorname{gp}^-(G),\operatorname{gp}^-(H)\}.
$$

The inequality has been verified for all pairs of graphs of order at most six, but remains open in general.

entry.title: The asymptotic generating-triple count conjecture for prefix reversals
entry.statement:
For $n$ and integers $m,k$ with $2\leqslant k<m<n$, let $f(n)$ be the number of pairs $(m,k)$ for which the prefix reversals $r_n,r_m,r_k$ generate the symmetric group $\operatorname{Sym}_n$. **Generating-triple count conjecture.** As $n$ tends to infinity, 
$$
f(n)=\begin{cases} \frac{1}{13}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv0\pmod{4},\\[6pt] \frac{1}{9}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv1\pmod{4},\\[6pt] \frac{1}{10}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv2\pmod{4},\\[6pt] \frac{1}{7}n^2+O(n)&n\equiv3\pmod{4}. \end{cases}
$$
 This is based on computational experiments for $6\leqslant n\leqslant70$; the source provides no proof or resolution.

entry.title: Circulant graph conjecture for monophonic position number two
entry.statement: Let $n$ be an integer, and let a **circulant graph** mean a graph whose vertices are arranged cyclically with adjacency determined by a fixed set of cyclic differences. The monophonic position number is denoted by $a$, and the diameter by $D$. **Circulant graph conjecture.** For any $n\geq 11$, there is a circulant graph with order $n$, monophonic position number $a=2$, and diameter $D=2$. The preceding theorem establishes existence of some graph with these parameters if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5,8\}$ or $n\geq 11$; the conjecture strengthens the large-order existence assertion by requiring the graph to be circulant, based on computational evidence.
